self                  → owner-only (requires user_id column); admins bypass. Declared `self` stays owner-only on a table that ALSO has the groups: key (tenant clause AND'd: your own rows in your effective tenant). For a user with NO tenant a declared `self` is plain owner scope: they reach every row whose user_id is theirs, whatever tenant it names - the one mode that does, per action, so declare it for rows a non-member owns on purpose (a join request) and not for tenant content (scoping.missing_group). Only the IMPLICIT default for a user_id + tenant-key table (no access: rule for it) is tenant-wide, and it needs the tenant: with none, only the user's rows that carry no tenant. On a table with neither user_id nor the groups: key there is nothing to scope by, so `self` (declared, or through `default:`) answers 404 to everyone but admins - declare everyone/role:/admin for such a table.
group                 → same-group only via groups: config; admins bypass. On a table with neither the groups: key nor user_id, `group` answers 404 to everyone but admins.

admin                 → only a global admin (users.role = admin or a global admin grant) can hit the endpoint at all. This holds in an app whose roles: block does not declare `admin` too (see api({at:'rbac'}))

role:<X>              → user holds role X (admins always bypass). On a table WITHOUT the groups: key column only a GLOBALLY held role counts (users.role or a grant with no group_id): a tenant membership role or tenant-scoped grant would reach every tenant's rows, so it gets 404 there. Exception: on the tenant root (groups.bootstrap.org_table without the key column) a tenant role reads/updates/deletes only the caller's own tenant row (id = your group) and cannot create org rows. A reference catalog every tenant shares (no per-tenant rows) can be listed under `groups.shared: [table]`; tenant roles keep passing role: gates on those tables. Rows: role: decides WHO may call, not which rows - see role_mode_rows: on a table with user_id and no groups: key a holder reaches only rows they own, so use owner_or_role:<X> when holders should reach every row.
role:<a>,<b>,<c>      → any-of: user holds at least one of the listed roles

owner_or_role:<r1,r2> → TIERED visibility in ONE declaration: owner sees own rows (user_id), a holder of any listed role sees their whole GROUP (group-keyed tables) or ALL rows (un-grouped), a platform admin sees everything. Replaces the `read: off` + hand-written secure-read flow that branched WHERE on user.role - exactly the 'owner sees own, manager sees group, admin sees all' shape. On a group-keyed table a role-holder with no tenant gets no role tier and, like every caller with no tenant, reaches only their own rows that carry no tenant (scoping.missing_group), so the mode never leaks across tenants. On an un-grouped table only a GLOBALLY held role widens to all rows; a role held only through a tenant membership or tenant-scoped grant sees its own rows there. Creating needs the owner tier: on a table WITHOUT a user_id column there is no row to own, so a create takes a listed role, judged exactly like role:<r1,r2> (a GLOBAL one on a table without the groups: key). Declare `write: everyone` when any signed-in user should create rows. On a table with user_id and no groups: key, owner_or_role:X gives holders of X every row while role:X leaves them only their own (role_mode_rows).

perm:<res>.<action>   → granular scope check against the user's UNIONED scope set across every held role after inherits: expansion. write implies read; *:* is full access. Requires a `roles:` block in the same app.yaml: without one no role grants any permission, so `perm:` refuses everyone and the write gate rejects the file. In an app with groups:, on a table WITHOUT the groups: key column only a permission granted by a GLOBALLY held role counts, exactly like role: (a tenant membership role or tenant-scoped grant would reach every tenant's rows, so it gets 404 there); on the tenant root it reaches only the caller's own tenant row and cannot create, and groups.shared tables keep counting tenant roles. Rows follow role: (see role_mode_rows): on a table with user_id and no groups: key a holder of the permission reaches only rows they own. See api({at:'rbac'}).

member-of:<mt>(<jc>,<uc>) → membership-scoped: rows visible only to users with a row in membership table <mt> pointing at them - the 'visible to members of this room/channel/project' shape. See member_of below.
off                   → endpoint returns 404 even to admins
